description: JVM memory, garbage collection, threads and classes for the database nodes, broken out per node so builds with different JDKs or collectors can be compared side by side.

panels.description: Recent CPU utilization reported by the JVM itself, as a fraction of the machine.
panels.title: JVM CPU Utilization

panels.description: rate of jvm_cpu_time_seconds_total, so one unit is one fully busy core. jvm_cpu_count is the ceiling for the node.
panels.title: JVM CPU Time (cores consumed)

panels.description: Whole-heap totals. Used and committed sum across heap pools. The limit uses max for the reason given on Heap Utilization: ZGC repeats the whole-heap limit on every generation.
panels.title: Heap Used / Committed / Limit

panels.description: Heap used as a share of the heap limit. Used is summed over heap pools; the limit is taken with max, not sum, because Generational ZGC reports the whole-heap limit on both the young and the old pool while G1 reports it only on the old generation.

targets.expr:
100 * sum by (host_name) (jvm_memory_used_bytes{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host", jvm_memory_type="heap"})
  / max by (host_name) (jvm_memory_limit_bytes{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host", jvm_memory_type="heap"})

panels.title: Heap Utilization

panels.description: Heap still occupied immediately after the last collection. This is the real working set: if it climbs steadily the node is retaining more, not merely allocating faster.
panels.title: Live Set After Last GC

panels.description: Client latency next to the GC panels below, so a pause spike and a latency spike can be lined up on the same time axis. These gauges are pre-aggregated per node and are never combined.
panels.title: Client Request Latency ${percentile} (${latency_unit:text})

panels.description: Per-pool heap usage. Pool names differ by collector: db0/db1 show G1 Eden / Survivor / Old Gen, db2 shows ZGC Young and Old Generation. That difference is the point of this panel.
panels.title: Heap Pools by Node

panels.description: Everything outside the heap: metaspace, compressed class space and the code cache segments.
panels.title: Non-Heap Used vs Committed

panels.description: Class metadata. Steady growth here without a matching class count rise points at a classloader leak.
panels.title: Metaspace and Compressed Class Space

panels.description: JIT-compiled code. If a segment reaches its limit the JVM stops compiling and throughput falls off with no other symptom.
panels.title: Code Cache (CodeHeap segments)
Garbage Collection — G1 on db0/db1, Generational ZGC on db2

panels.description: Collections per minute, split by the collector's own name. G1 nodes report G1 Young Generation; the ZGC node reports Major Cycles and Major Pauses separately.
panels.title: GC Rate by Collector

panels.description: Mean is _sum/_count and is exact. p99 comes from jvm_gc_duration_seconds_bucket, a real histogram, so histogram_quantile is valid; its default buckets are coarse, so read p99 as a bucket boundary.

targets.expr:
sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))
  / sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_count{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval]))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name, le) (rate(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_bucket{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: GC Duration by Collector — mean and p99

panels.description: Stop-the-world pause time as a share of wall clock, plus ZGC concurrent cycle time for reference. db0/db1 run G1 on JDK 11 and report only pauses; db2 runs Generational ZGC on JDK 21 and reports both, so the concurrent series exists only there.
panels.title: GC Time Overhead (% of wall clock)

panels.description: Total pause time divided by pause count across the whole dashboard range. Concurrent ZGC cycles are excluded so the number means the same thing on every node.

targets.expr:
sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (increase(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_sum{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__range]))
  / sum by (host_name, jvm_gc_name) (increase(jvm_gc_duration_seconds_count{job="cassandra", host_name=~"$host", jvm_gc_name!~".*Cycles"}[$__range]))

panels.title: Mean GC Pause over the selected range

panels.description: Total live threads. jvm_thread_count is split by daemon flag and state, so it must be summed.
panels.title: JVM Threads by Node

panels.description: Runnable against waiting and timed_waiting. A jump in runnable threads with flat throughput means contention rather than work.
panels.title: Threads by State

panels.description: Sustained loading long after startup usually means dynamic class generation.
panels.title: Class Load / Unload Rate

list.description: Which pre-aggregated latency gauge to read. The gauges are computed per node; they are never summed or averaged across nodes.
list.label: Percentile
list.name: percentile

list.description: Display unit for latency. The metric is emitted in microseconds, so the value is the divisor: milliseconds divides by 1000, microseconds divides by 1.
list.label: Latency unit
list.name: latency_unit

list.description: Database nodes only. Derived from a Cassandra-only metric, so control and app nodes never appear.
list.label: Host
list.name: host

title: Cassandra JVM Internals
